import_original.title: Import from {original_name}
import_original.description:
Moves the vacuum's settings, map options, Xiaomi cloud session, device and entities here from {original_name}. Entity ids stay the same, so dashboards and automations keep working.

Its entry in {original_name} is disabled (you can enable it again); nothing is deleted. Afterwards you can delete that entry and uninstall {original_name}.

import_original_confirm.title: Import {name}
import_original_confirm.description:
{name} is set up in {original_name}. Move its settings, map options, Xiaomi cloud session, device and entities here? Entity ids stay the same.

Its entry in {original_name} is disabled (you can enable it again); nothing is deleted.

reauth_captcha.title: Xiaomi asked for a captcha
reauth_captcha.description:
The Xiaomi Cloud session for {name} expired and could not be renewed automatically. When Home Assistant tried to log in again with the saved password, Xiaomi asked for a captcha, which only you can solve.

Submit to continue: you'll log in again and see the captcha image.

reauth_verification.title: Xiaomi asked to verify your account
reauth_verification.description:
The Xiaomi Cloud session for {name} expired and could not be renewed automatically. When Home Assistant tried to log in again with the saved password, Xiaomi asked to verify that it's you.

1. Open [this verification page]({verification_url}) on a device connected to the same network (same public IP) as Home Assistant and complete the verification.
2. Come back and submit to log in again.

progress.wait_for_login:
Scan the QR code with the Xiaomi Home app and approve the login there, or open [this link]({login_link}) on your phone or computer and sign in to your Xiaomi account. The code is valid for a few minutes.

Configuring {integration_title} using YAML is being removed.

Your existing YAML configuration has been imported into the UI automatically.

Remove the `{domain}` camera from your configuration.yaml file and restart Home Assistant to fix this issue.
deprecated_yaml.title: The {integration_title} YAML configuration is being removed

original_left.title: {name} moved from Xiaomi Cloud Map Extractor
original_left.description:
{name} now runs in Better Xiaomi Cloud Map Extractor with the same device and entity ids. Its entry in Xiaomi Cloud Map Extractor is disabled and no longer needed.

To finish switching, delete the disabled Xiaomi Cloud Map Extractor entry under Settings > Devices & services (the device and entities stay here), then uninstall Xiaomi Cloud Map Extractor.

original_left_yaml.title: {name} moved from Xiaomi Cloud Map Extractor
original_left_yaml.description:
{name} now runs in Better Xiaomi Cloud Map Extractor with the same device and entity ids. Its entry in Xiaomi Cloud Map Extractor is disabled and no longer needed.

To finish switching, in this order:

1. Remove the `xiaomi_cloud_map_extractor` camera from `{file}` (line {line}) and restart Home Assistant. The repair **Remove the old Xiaomi Cloud Map Extractor YAML** shows the exact block. If the original is uninstalled while the block is still there, Home Assistant reports an error at every start.
2. Delete the disabled Xiaomi Cloud Map Extractor entry under Settings > Devices & services (the device and entities stay here).
3. Uninstall Xiaomi Cloud Map Extractor.

original_yaml.title: Remove the old Xiaomi Cloud Map Extractor YAML for {name}
original_yaml.description:
{name} now runs in Better Xiaomi Cloud Map Extractor, but `{file}` still sets it up for the original Xiaomi Cloud Map Extractor, starting at line {line}:

{snippet}

Removing this block is safe: Better Xiaomi Cloud Map Extractor does not read it, and the device, entities and settings stay as they are. Without the original installed, the block makes Home Assistant report "Integration 'xiaomi_cloud_map_extractor' not found" at every start.

Delete this `- platform: xiaomi_cloud_map_extractor` item from `{file}` (and the `camera:` line, if nothing else is under it), then restart Home Assistant. The username, password and token are hidden above; your file may show them or use `!secret`.

Select **Submit** to switch to the {detected_api} map format and reload the integration. Your entities, options and login stay as they are.

vacuum.title: Vacuum address and token
vacuum.description:
{name} has not answered at {host} for 5 minutes, so Home Assistant can't tell when it cleans. Its IP address or token may have changed (new router lease, reset, re-pairing in the Xiaomi Home app).

Enter its IP address and token. The values filled in come from Xiaomi Cloud when it could be reached, otherwise they are the stored ones. If they are already right, check that the vacuum is on and on the same network as Home Assistant; this goes away by itself once it answers. If Home Assistant can't reach the vacuum on purpose (another network or VLAN), close this window and choose Ignore on the repair.
